surfaceForm: Pattern: eduroam <-> TAC-aware Wi-Fi ... the institution's eduroam participation continues for inter-institutional roaming ... Visiting researchers receive the default eduroam treatment
proposedGenericDecision: eduroam is a near-universal R&E federated-Wi-Fi service (100+ countries) and is a legitimate generic reference for any university; it is not UL-bound and should be kept. However, the section implicitly assumes the institution is an eduroam participant with peer-institution roaming and a national/regional R&E identity-federation context. For a fully institution-agnostic statement, frame eduroam participation as a conditional ('institutions participating in eduroam') rather than as an assumed given.
rationale: eduroam itself is genuinely generic (documented in the project's it-policy-domain rules as a cross-country R&E service). The only implicit specificity is the unstated assumption of eduroam membership, which most but not all adopters share; soft 'keep' with a framing caveat rather than parameterize.

surfaceForm: the hybrid Shibboleth--Keycloak identity arrangement is a legitimate end-state, for example
location: ch30-coexistence-patterns-EN.tex / sec:cp-anti-patterns (Common anti-patterns), Coexistence as a permanent feature
proposedGenericDecision: A concrete named product pairing used as an illustrative example of a legitimate permanent-coexistence end-state. Shibboleth and Keycloak are generic open-source IdP products (not UL-specific), so the example is portable; keep as an illustrative instance, or generalize to 'a hybrid SAML-IdP / OIDC-IdP identity arrangement' if a product-neutral phrasing is preferred for agnosticism.
rationale: Shibboleth and Keycloak are widely-deployed generic products, consistent with the chapter's convention of naming third-party tooling. Not institution-specific. Listed for completeness because it is a concrete tooling exemplar that an agnostic editor might want product-neutralised; default is keep.

surfaceForm: a coexistence that has not been revisited in twenty-four months is reviewed
location: ch30-coexistence-patterns-EN.tex / sec:cp-anti-patterns (Common anti-patterns), Coexistence as a permanent feature
proposedGenericDecision: A 24-month periodic-review interval tied to 'the sovereignty grid'. This is a named design constant of the playbook's governance cadence, not a jurisdiction-bound figure. Keep as a design constant of the framework (consistent with the project's policy of keeping named design constants), or parameterize the interval if adopters set their own review cadence.
rationale: Per the project's abstract-over-quantitative-selfrefs guidance, named design constants are retained. The 24-month interval is a framework design choice, not UL-specific or jurisdiction-bound. Low-confidence flag in case adopters want it parameterized.
